newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chances of Brazil CVRD auction today slim - bidder.
newsitem.headline: Chances of Brazil CVRD auction today slim - bidder.

text.p: The chances of the auction of Brazilian mining giant CVRD going ahead today are slim, said the chief executive of consortium leader Votorantim.
Antonio Ermirio de Moraes said it was more likely the auction of a 45 percent voting stake in CVRD would take place in May.
"Anything is possible, but everything points toward the auction taking place in May," he said. "We are waiting here patiently for the court to take its decision."
The government was scheduled to sell a 45 percent voting stake in CVRD on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange Tuesday morning, but a flurry of court injunctions has suspended the auction.

Moraes said the legal battles surrounding the CVRD privatization came as no surprise. He said they were typical of all privatizations and even more likely to occur with a company like CVRD which deals with an unrenewable resource like iron ore.
He said foreign investors participating in his Valecom consortium were not concerned by the auction delay and everyone was confident the auction would take place eventually.

Valecom includes South Africa's Anglo-American Corp, a group of 11 Japanese steelmakers and trading companies, two pension funds and Brazilian metal and metallurgical group Caemi, which is 40 percent owned by Japan's Mitsui & Co.
Moraes said Votorantim and Anglo-American each has a 41.5 percent stake in the consortium, while Caemi and the group of Japanese investors each hold an 8.5 percent stake in the consortium.
He said if Valecom won the auction, it would take at least 60 days to study CVRD thouroughly before taking any decisions on what changes would be made in the privatized company.
One of the first areas to be restructured would be CVRD's aluminium business which was the least profitable with debt of around $2 billion, Moraes said.
He said the aluminium operations would be unified to make them more efficient.
Moraes rejected accusations that his metal, cement and pulp group was trying to concentrate power in its hands.

"The CVRD stake will be administered by a professional team of executives and decisions will be taken democratically," he said. "The important thing is to keep the center of decision-making on CVRD within Brazil."
Moraes would become chairman of the special purpose company which would administer the 45 percent CVRD stake should Valecom win the auction.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
